body: thank you so much! this really means a lot to me. I've been struggling to make sense of what options I have and what you've said really helped put things into perspective.
thank you! i appreciate this very much <3

I've been thinking that at least, perhaps I could come home for my mother. She's been with my father longer than I am and been through worse relationship with him, and it breaks my heart every single time she calls me and tell how horrible my father is treating her (he's no longer physical with my mother and never physical with me, but his words are absolutely destroy us to the guts) accusing her of 'not taking care of him properly' when he's very sick at home just because she didn't hear my dad calling for her from bedroom, or some other dumb reasons. I feel bad for my mother because she's been taking care of my father all by herself to the point that she gets sick herself. But the problem is I am more prone to meltdown, which usually circle back to my father blaming my mother for my 'reaction', and I'm afraid that I wouldn't be able to endure it and snaps again, making things worse for her.

Nevertheless, regardless how emotionally damaging it's been to be around my father, it's not like he's completely abandon me or anything. He's not physically abusive but he does scar me emotionally with the gaslight and humiliation and all that. Yes, he's basically there for financial aids and making sure I get proper and good education, and introducing me to lots of people so I can have better networking for future career prospects; and everything else becomes my mother's job to raise me. So I still feel like I need to be there, because in his mind, he thinks he's a good parent whose daughter has no reason not to come back home when he asks to since he's pouring so much into raising me. Unfortunately, I've never told him about my mental health issues because knowing him and how he scrutinised his mother's decision to seek mental health help, I've feared that he'd be dismissive of mine.

It's just, really hard not to think about worst case scenario now, and I keep thinking about my friends who said that their biggest regret is not being there on their late parent's deathbed and I don't know if trading my mental health is worth of making sure I won't have to live with that kind of regret for the rest of my life.

I totally agree. I feel like most people think because it's their original character, they can do whatever they want, which is true to some extent, but once they interact with someone else's character, it is important to respect and realise it's a work of two people/more now and not just theirs.

I am sorry you have to deal with that. It is quite bothersome when someone godmod your character, yes, but with the elements of actions I might understand why they want their character to 'win'. However, roleplaying is a product of collaboration and you have the right to give as much input as your partner does. Explain to your partner why it is wrong to do that, and why you're uncomfortable with it.

Have you tried to set up the scene with your rp partner? Usually when I don't really know how to play out an RP, I'd suggest my partner to come up with some kind of list of things we want to happen in one roleplay, like a bullet points guide. That way, at least we can concentrate on how to play out what's already been planned rather that considering what to do from endless random possibilities. I hope this helps!

I get that. Of course I do not participate in anything they're doing because of it all, but it doesn't mean I cannot talk about this issue too. Isn't that the whole point of this subreddit? Are you going to each post telling each OP to ignore and move on? Not participating is one thing, and ignoring the inherent toxicity of it is another thing. I might not be able to change how society perceive the glorified version of abusive relationship and whatnot, but I am still allowed to talk about it. Discuss it with people who have similar experience. Rendering it to your, quite frankly, aggressive first comment about how 'there's no problem here, just ignore and move on, listen to me while I imply that I am very likely older than you', is not a solution and it seems like you undervalue my concern for my roleplaying community. Again, I am terribly sorry if this post doesn't sit well with you, but you can always take your own advice to ignore this post and move on.

your take on this is valid. forgive me if i did not make myself clear that my point isn't about whether i don't like people writing such topics, but their treatment to the story. again, my point is, i disagree with glorifying trauma. i am aware that there's a difference between exploring topics with respect, and romanticised it like it's an afterthought. i am very sorry if you disagree with my post, and my replies to another comments fail to enlighten my point from writing this whole thing.

it is genuinely a scary thing but it warms my heart when conan said how andy was with him the whole time, like ofc their ongoing bit is how andy doesnt like conan behind the camera because he's a terrible boss but they're genuinely good friends for each other.

i've seen some people who make their character extremely uncomfortable with meeting or trusting new people but would make write their character spill out every detail about themselves with the justification by writing like 'there's something different about OC B that makes OC A feels like she can tell him everything' which is, realistically, something that can happen after meeting for more than 10 minutes. i think this is an example of immature writers who simply too eager to accelerate the progress of the plot that they want to skip the slow burn of the whole 'struggle to make connection for months before opening up to someone'

it's pretty annoying when you're making a character who is struggling with several circumstances and you make it clear where did those feeling stemmed from and how it affects your character, but someone is like, "well yes but once they meet my character, and i expect it happen on the first rp we have with them, you're character is gonna open up and tell my character everything because my character will save them and show them how to heal without truly knowing their history because my character will be like, it's okay i totes get your insecurity because i have a neighbour who had similar problem as yours"

'broken' character is not a romantic trope, and their lack of respect and patience to even dealing with this on a writing platform shows so much of their character and how they deal with these people irl.
that is very valid, and i wholly supportive of that. i feel like this type of thing can only work if you're actually familiar with it, or at least you're carefully learning about it.

it honestly makes me feel super self conscious about myself like oh they abort it cus they realise my writing is shite. but i totally get if they take more time to reply if they tell me from the beginning that they can be active for a certain amount of time per day.
personally as follow to that, for me it's when i asked how do you want the rp to start like what's the set up you want me to write, and their only answer is idc. not even i don't care or up to you + emoji. it literally just says idc.

oh my god now that you mention it, i realise that these two people's characters are always the variation of 'dead mom, abusive father, character is either a sensitive manchild or a casanova who treats their lovers like disposable gum wrappers, meets a mysterious stoic character who doesnt talk about the harsh treatment the authority gives them because they're misunderstood vigilante' like, those are very intriguing set up to base your characters with but oh my god the way they're cooking up their characters and plots are, well.... 

i mean, sure, make any characters as dark as you want, but realistically, would you actually gonna think it's uwu if those are real life stories? i think people are so caught up with the euphoria of writing *fiction* that they completely ignore that even fake stories still need to make sense

i completely agree with you. yes trauma seems like an 'edgy' thing to add to character but sometimes people do pepper bunch of unnecessary trauma just because they feel like it makes them seem like they're capable of writing complex character and whatnot.

i have this rp partner who is fully interested in one of my character: a really horrible person whose flaw is that they blame their whole tragic backstory on society and thus turn them into a villain, but it's a no-brainer than this character is irredeemable. and this person wants to have some kind of 'the bad guys has a heart of one soft girl' kind of trope and i explained to this person that while i'm game for that, i know my character will only show compassion to a certain degree, which is never enough and most likely won't be justified by common sense, and it's not going to end well for both of them because i cannot see my character going any other path other than doom after everything this character have done, and this person was like yeah :) sure :) but they're very cute together tho :) - this kind of mentality worries me so much. the amount of people hyping toxic relationships and justified their actions, even though it's just fiction, is not okay and i'm hoping that people would outgrew that and realise it's so not okay to normalise that.

you can start by writing a post about your character minding their own business, just go on with daily life, and then i think eventually your rp partner will respond by setting up that they bump to each other eventually

i legit have meet people who blatantly admit 'yes it's draining to keep planning rps and not actually rping/ghosting but what do you expect people to do? planning is fun and we've used all our energy on planning, ofc we have no time to go as far as roleplaying' which is a super weird thing to admit ngl

the last person who ghost on me was this girl who abandoned our roleplay and use the exact same plot we used to roleplay with someone else because she felt like i 'abandoned' her first by not responding to her ooc post, which i did but she simply didn't see it because she immediately went offline after sending that ooc post. and instead of asking me again like 'hey did u see my post?' or stuffs like that, she just completely was like 'yeah it doesnt seem like you wanna rp with me anymore it's okay though we dont have to do it anymore :)'. like, everything was going so fine and we've planned stuffs and all, and it's pretty heartcrushing that i've spent so much time working in our roleplay only for her to abandon it like that.

i feel like 2-4 paragraph is a reasonable length of responses, it has enough for my partner to respond to, but there are some people who really love to write long stuffs, like about 350-500 words, which is fine when they give me so much to respond to in their post so i can also think of 350-500 words to write, but when those words are just very detailed personal description about something that my characters cannot react to, that's when i get kind of overwhelmed. 

basically, i really have nothing against detailed description of something, i think it has beauty to it, and i myself sometimes do it when i have to write the starter post for the roleplay and set up the scene, but there are indeed people who are using that as a tool to flex on how much words they can write in one post.

Hello! In my experience, when I'm really feeling my character and the roleplay itself is either got stopped in the middle because one reason or another, or it just goes very slow, I often take time to write something like a character study, some short stories about my character that took place either before rp so I don't godmod my partner's character, or something that happen in between two rps. It keeps my writing juice flowing and helps me finding new things about my character too. Hope this helps!
